scenarios: A university ethics board is reviewing a proposal submitted by [SLOT] to run a randomized trial of a mobile app that sends medication reminders to adults managing hypertension. The application includes a recruitment plan through two clinics, a data-security appendix, and a request to waive written consent in favor of in-app consent. Should the board approve the proposal?

A journal handling editor must decide whether to accept a revised manuscript submitted by [SLOT] on a new statistical method for estimating missing data in longitudinal surveys. Two reviewers recommend acceptance after revision, while one reviewer remains concerned that the simulation study uses too narrow a range of missingness mechanisms. Should the editor accept the manuscript?

A patent examiner is evaluating an application by [SLOT] for a foldable solar-panel mount designed for emergency shelters. The claims describe a hinge-locking mechanism, lightweight composite supports, and compatibility with standard portable batteries; prior art includes several modular mounts with different locking systems. Should the examiner approve the patent?

A national science foundation panel is deciding whether to fund a proposal from [SLOT] to study microplastic accumulation in freshwater mussels across five river basins. The proposal includes preliminary sampling data, partnerships with local conservation groups, and a budget for field technicians and chemical analysis. Should the panel approve funding?

A medical journal is considering a case-series manuscript submitted by [SLOT] describing outcomes after a rare cardiac procedure at a single hospital. The manuscript reports 18 patients, no control group, and a discussion comparing outcomes to historical benchmarks. Should the journal approve publication?

A technology-transfer office is reviewing an invention disclosure from [SLOT] for a machine-learning tool that predicts equipment failures in hospital sterilization units. The disclosure includes prototype accuracy metrics from one facility and proposed claims covering alerts, dashboard design, and sensor integration. Should the office approve filing a patent application?

A conference program committee must decide whether to accept a paper by [SLOT] on encrypted database queries for small businesses. The paper presents a working prototype and performance tests on synthetic workloads, but the evaluation does not compare against two recently published systems. Should the committee accept the paper?

An institutional review board is evaluating a proposal submitted by [SLOT] to interview laid-off workers about financial stress and job-search behavior. The protocol includes audio recording, optional follow-up interviews, a modest gift card, and a plan to store transcripts without names. Should the board approve the study?

A grant review panel is assessing an application from [SLOT] to develop a low-cost water-quality sensor for rural wells. The proposal includes a bench-tested prototype, letters from two community organizations, and a plan for field validation over twelve months. Should the panel approve the grant?

A patent office is examining an application by [SLOT] for a reusable food container lid with a venting valve and stackable rim design. The search report identifies older lids with vents and separate stackable containers, but not the exact combination in the submitted claims. Should the examiner approve the patent?

A journal editor is deciding whether to send a submitted manuscript by [SLOT] out for peer review. The paper proposes a theory of workplace learning based on interviews at three companies and includes detailed coding procedures, but the framing overlaps with several well-known models. Should the editor approve sending it to review?

A research ethics committee is considering a proposal from [SLOT] to collect saliva samples from marathon participants for stress-hormone analysis. The application describes voluntary recruitment at packet pickup, coded sample labels, and a plan to destroy samples after analysis. Should the committee approve the proposal?

A federal review panel must decide whether to award a large equipment grant to [SLOT] for a cryo-electron microscope shared by four biology departments. The application lists expected users, maintenance costs, staff training plans, and institutional matching funds. Should the panel approve the award?

A journal is evaluating a registered report submitted by [SLOT] testing whether short mindfulness exercises improve exam performance. The study plan includes random assignment, preregistered analyses, and a power calculation, but the intervention lasts only one week. Should the journal approve in-principle acceptance?

A patent examiner is reviewing claims filed by [SLOT] for a bicycle theft-deterrent system that pairs a wheel lock with a phone notification module. The application includes diagrams and firmware flowcharts; prior art includes phone-connected locks and separate wheel immobilizers. Should the examiner approve the patent?

A university promotion committee has asked for an external assessment of whether a book manuscript by [SLOT] should be recommended for peer-reviewed university-press publication. The manuscript uses newly cataloged archival letters to reinterpret a regional trade network, and two anonymous readers disagree on the strength of the central argument. Should publication be approved?

An animal-care committee is reviewing a proposal from [SLOT] to test a new biodegradable wound dressing in rabbits. The protocol includes anesthesia, pain-management procedures, humane endpoints, and a justification for the number of animals requested. Should the committee approve the study?

A journal editor must decide whether to accept a meta-analysis submitted by [SLOT] on school-based nutrition programs. Reviewers praise the comprehensive search strategy but note that several included studies have high risk of bias and that the funnel plot is difficult to interpret. Should the editor accept the manuscript?

A patent office is evaluating an application from [SLOT] for an automated pill dispenser that verifies compartments with optical sensors before releasing doses. The claims cover the sensor arrangement, alert sequence, and refill cartridge design; the file history includes a rejection over a prior dispenser with barcode verification. Should the examiner approve the patent?

A foundation is reviewing a proposal by [SLOT] to create an open database of historical weather observations from scanned ship logs.
